title: Run-of-play term reads the whole innings on legal ball 19
description: In _shock_and_delta the 18-ball window is wicket_sum[end] - wicket_sum[end-18]. At position 18 (legal ball 19) end-18 = -1, and numpy index -1 is the LAST element, so the window subtracts the innings total. Ball 19 therefore uses future balls of the same innings, and the extreme values inflate the SD used to scale every other ball.
evidence: Replicated exactly (max gap 0). Ball 19 mean run of play: batter 0.983 (bug-free 0.076), bowler 1.000 (bug-free 0.251). Scale: runs 1.1072 vs bug-free 0.5928; wickets 0.0830 vs 0.0733. Ball 19 bowler high-band share 54.9% vs 20% design.
affected_outputs: pressure_bat, pressure_bowl, band, band_bowl, every band and clutch component
quantified_impact: Diagnostic rescoring with the bug removed: batters Spearman 0.998, top-20 overlap 20/20; bowlers Spearman 0.958, top-20 overlap 14/20. Band agreement batters 98.9%, bowlers 95.0%.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Guard the 18-ball window for end-18 < 0 (subtract 0), then rebuild ratings.

title: Deck export 10 labels final shock as 'count_shock'
description: write_deck_exports writes sample['shock_bat'] and sample['shock_bowl'] into columns named count_shock_bat / count_shock_bowl. After _add_expected_shock those columns hold count + excess shock, not the count part.
evidence: exports/10_sample_innings_timeline.csv count_shock_bat equals final shock: True; equals count part: False.
affected_outputs: exports/10_sample_innings_timeline.csv and any slide built from it
quantified_impact: Labels only; values are the shock actually used. 06_shock/shock_innings_timeline.csv splits count, excess and final.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Rename the columns or write both parts.

title: Bowler clutch compares spell economy without extras to career economy with extras
description: In score_bowlers the high-band spell economy uses charged_runs on legal balls (wides and no-balls are not legal rows), while the career economy it is compared with uses conceded on all deliveries (wides and no-ball runs included). A spell is therefore flattered by the bowler's own wide/no-ball rate.
evidence: Ranked bowlers: career economy with extras minus legal-balls-only economy = 0.369 runs/over on average = 0.107 clutch-scale units (scale 3.433). High-band spells counted as beating the bowler's own rate: 36.5% as executed vs 32.9% on a like-for-like basis.
quantified_impact: Shifts every bowler's own gap upward by their wide/no-ball rate; ranking effect not re-estimated (would require changing the method).
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Use the same delivery basis on both sides of the comparison.

title: Form term used a full-career bar (look-ahead)
description: Legacy form_by_season (git HEAD) compared each of the previous 8 innings with the player's FULL-CAREER strike rate/economy, which includes later matches.
evidence: Source at git 29956ed: bar = float(career.loc[player]) with career = strike_rate/economy over all seasons. The current working tree removes Form entirely (7 terms, consistency 0.10).
quantified_impact: Legacy 8-term vs current 7-term: batters Spearman 0.989, top-20 overlap 18; bowlers Spearman 0.991, top-20 overlap 18.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: If Form returns, use a point-in-time bar.

title: xWicket is trained on bowler wickets but charged against every striker dismissal
description: Wicket cells learn bowler_wicket (caught, bowled, LBW, stumped, hit wicket). The batter ball value subtracts 4 x (striker_out - xW), and striker_out includes run outs, retired out and obstructing. Non-striker dismissals hit nobody's ball value.
evidence: Legal balls: striker_out 10,555 vs bowler_wicket 10,236; striker run outs 314; non-striker dismissals 265. Mean xW 5.13% vs striker-out rate 5.49% and bowler-wicket rate 5.32%. Mean wicket part of ball value: batter -0.0142, bowler 0.0076 per ball.
affected_outputs: e_bat, batter Elo, batter band components
quantified_impact: Batter wicket penalty is biased by about -0.0142 runs-equivalent per ball overall; concentrated on batters involved in run outs.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Train a striker-dismissal expectation, or exclude run outs from the batter wicket term.

title: No wickets-fallen feature in the expectation model
description: Expectation cells are ladder x phase x arm (plus the Elo gap). Wickets already down are not a key, although they change scoring and dismissal rates.
evidence: Runs actual minus expected per ball: 0-1 down 0.084, 2-3 down 0.018, 4-5 down -0.011, 6-7 down -0.104, 8-9 down -0.345. Mean batter ball value at 8-9 down -0.421 on 6,621 balls.
affected_outputs: e_bat, e_bowl, Elo, all band components
quantified_impact: Batters at the top of an innings are credited, tail batters penalised; bowlers who bowl to tails gain. Batters are z-scored within order groups, which absorbs part of this for batters; bowlers are pooled.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Add a wickets-down key (e.g. 0-1, 2-4, 5-7, 8+) to the cells.

title: Wides and no-balls never enter the ball value or Elo
description: Charging follows the laws in `conceded` (wide: all runs; no-ball: no-ball run + bat runs). But ball value, Elo, xR, bands and clutch use legal rows only, so wide and no-ball runs and wickets off wides are invisible there. Baseline economy and peers include them.
evidence: 11,265 of 279,510 conceded runs (4.0%) are on illegal deliveries; 25 bowler wickets (stumpings off wides) are credited in baseline only.
affected_outputs: e_bowl, bowler Elo, bowler bands, bowler clutch
quantified_impact: A wayward bowler is penalised only in baseline (0.20) and peers (0.10).
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Attach illegal-delivery runs to the next legal ball or model them separately.

title: High pressure is, in practice, the six balls after a wicket (batters) or a boundary (bowlers)
description: The excess-wicket shock sits at its -0.5 floor whenever no wicket fell in the last six balls and near +1 after one; the base context term is small, so the top-20% cut is crossed almost only after a wicket. For bowlers the analogous trigger is a four/six or runs above expectation.
evidence: 99.94% of batter high-band balls are within 6 balls after a wicket; 0.018% of other balls are high. 99.98% of bowler high-band balls follow a four or six in the previous six. Variance share of the occasion x competition x ball term: batters 7.1%, bowlers 3.1%.
quantified_impact: Occasion (final vs league) moves the high-band share only from 21.3% to 26.1%.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Present the high band as 'after a wicket / after being hit', or rebalance the terms.

title: The first 18 balls of an innings are almost never high pressure
description: Shock needs six previous balls and run of play needs eighteen, so the opening three overs rarely reach the cut.
evidence: Batter high-band share on balls 1-18: 0.04% vs 25.1% from ball 19; bowlers 4.2% on balls 1-18.
affected_outputs: opening batters' and new-ball bowlers' high-band samples
quantified_impact: Openers face the high band only after early wickets.

title: Median batter pressure is negative
description: The batter excess-wicket term is negative whenever no wicket fell recently.
evidence: Batter p50 = -0.050; excess term at -0.5 floor on 50.7% of balls; final shock negative on 68.4%.

title: Normalisation uses the full 2022-2026 sample
description: Band cut-offs, z-score reference pools, and the shock/run-of-play scales are computed on all seasons, so they are not point-in-time. Per-ball xR/xW and Elo are sequential and do not look ahead.
evidence: Code reading: _cut_band quantiles, zscore reference, std scales over full frame.
quantified_impact: Fine for a retrospective ranking; not valid as a live/forecast metric.

title: Season decay applies to some components only
description: 0.9^(2026-season) weights the band rates and n_eff. Baseline rates, peers, clutch and consistency are level-weighted only.
evidence: Code reading: career_rate/weighted_count vs _weighted_mean and raw totals.
quantified_impact: Older seasons count fully in 0.55 of the weight.

title: Top bowlers sit close to the sample floor
description: Eligibility is n_eff >= 120 and high-band n_eff >= 30. Several top bowlers have small high-band samples, and z-scores are capped at +-3 rather than shrunk further.
evidence: Median high-band n_eff: top-20 bowlers 85.7 vs all ranked 92.8; 4 of the top-10 bowlers have high n_eff < 60. Humphreys high n_eff 31.3; Bosch 367 legal balls.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Report intervals or a stricter floor for headline lists.

title: Expectation models discriminate weakly
description: xR and xW are cell means with an Elo tilt.
evidence: xR: MAE 1.304 vs 1.328 for a constant; R^2 0.0133; calibration slope 0.985. xW (bowler wicket): AUC 0.559, Brier 0.05021 vs 0.05037 constant, logistic slope 0.806.
affected_outputs: ball value for every component except baseline
quantified_impact: Ball values are close to 'actual minus phase average'.

title: Consistency works against the composite for batters
description: Consistency rewards a low spread of match ball value; explosive batters score low.
evidence: Ranked batters: corr(consistency, composite) -0.195; corr(peers, consistency) -0.400. Cap share for consistency at +-3: 1.4%.
quantified_impact: Variance share of consistency in the batter composite -4.1%.

title: Lower-level events are discounted twice
description: Emerging/Rising balls count 0.5 (level weight) and also carry a 0.7 competition multiplier in pressure.
evidence: 6,720 legal balls in 30 matches.

title: Competition coverage
description: IPL 2022-2026, bilateral and tri-series T20Is, two Asia Cups and two A-team events. No T20 World Cup, no other franchise leagues. Tri-series and Asia Cup finals carry the same 3.0 occasion as an IPL final.
evidence: Matches with legal balls: IPL 367, T20I 470, T20 30.

title: DLS detail is limited

evidence: Reduced matches 34; chases with no supplied target (no required rate) 2 matches.

title: Source anomalies kept as supplied
description: Deliveries with a player missing from the squad sheet are kept; one over has more than six legal balls; three rows have extras amounts that do not fit the type.
evidence: sheet_gap deliveries 175; overs with >6 legal balls 1.

title: 'Other' extras are treated as illegal

evidence: 263 non-super-over 'other' deliveries.

title: Elo affects the ranking only through expectations
description: The composite is built from ball values; final Elo ratings are not a component.
evidence: Season-end rating stability (Spearman, keys with >=120 balls both seasons): batters 0.54-0.79, bowlers 0.44-0.74. Step-size sensitivity: composite Spearman >= 0.985.
